prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: square raster ALBEDO texture atlas for a painterly 3D game environment. Four by four EXACT equal cells, no labels or grid lines.
Input image: style reference only, showing the intended brushwork and shape grouping.
Primary request: A new GRAYSCALE material atlas matching the reference's broad deliberate pixel-paint clusters and painted surfaces. Flat orthographic UV textures only. No scene, no render of objects.
Critical visual style: 1990s background-painting meets carefully grouped pixel art. TWO TO FOUR LARGE PAINT TONES per material; beautiful irregular angular paint islands with occasional small stepped contours. Retain purposeful close-up wood grain and bark marks, yet broad quiet areas dominate. No photographic textures, no tiny noise, no crackle filter, no soft CGI gradients, no beveled cubes, no dramatic highlights, no circular vignette. Most pixels pale gray 78–97% brightness, secondary brush planes 60–75%; sparse deep marks 35–50%. Neutral gray colors everywhere, so vertex colors can tint each material.
Precisely arranged 4x4 cells:
TOP ROW: 1. quiet lime plaster, broad brush patches and scattered worn plaster edges, no cracks; 2. vertical old dark timber, broad long uneven grain stripes with tiny restrained splinters and a knot; 3. smoother vertically painted shutter wood with three broad grain bands, no plank assembly; 4. one clay roof shingle with a gently chipped lower edge, broad brush patches, no grid of tiles.
SECOND ROW: 5. old stone wall, 6 to 9 large roughly squared stones with a few small moss-like paint islands, shallow narrow dark joints; 6. ancient oak bark, LONG BROAD angular vertical grooves like calligraphic strokes, restrained small fissures, NO dense parallel hairlines; 7. quiet earth with widely spaced grouped angular limestone gravel patches and broad soil planes; 8. irregular worn paving stones with large quiet centers and broken polygonal edges.
THIRD ROW: 9. one broad stylized lobed oak leaf flat, subtle midrib, pale gray background; 10. one small oval shrub leaf flat with subtle veins; 11. one lanceolate leaf flat; 12. a small five-petal flower with broad simple shapes, pale gray background.
BOTTOM ROW: 13. broad angular moss and lichen islands; 14. old vertical door wood with clean broad grain, no hardware; 15. near-uniform pale old glass with only a little broad waviness; 16. SEAMLESS FOREST CANOPY LIGHT MASK: flat high-contrast dark gray irregular overlapping leafy silhouettes around bright gray sunlit openings, dense on 45 percent of the cell, open on 55 percent; grouped organic clusters with jagged stepped lobed edges, no branches, no diffuse texture. The mask is flat, evenly focused, without a surrounding border.
Layout: exact 25%, 50%, 75% cell boundaries, sixteen contiguous square cells, no gutters or margins. All textures aligned face-on. This sheet should look designed by an environment background painter, with clear organized shapes at thumbnail size and restrained intentional marks visible up close.
Constraints: grayscale only, no text, no symbols, no painted lighting direction on surfaces, no cast shadows except the explicit flat canopy mask in the last cell.
